title: Coverage doesn't work with long classpaths

labels.name: P2
labels.description: We'll consider working on this in future. (Assignee optional)

body:
### Description of the problem / feature request:

If the classpath for a test target exceeds the limit (specified at https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/fd5d29aa4ef907a15ec6db0e359e86df1acf64fc/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/bazel/rules/java/java_stub_template.txt#L358) the classpath is written to separate file, and coverage output is empty.

### Bugs: what's the simplest, easiest way to reproduce this bug? Please provide a minimal example if possible.

Clone bazel repo and run
```
$ bazel coverage //examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject:custom
...
//examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject:custom        PASSED in 0.7s
  /home/ubuntu/.cache/bazel/_bazel_ubuntu/5bb6c1fa5da68b7db1883687715859ce/execroot/io_bazel/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/testlogs/examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject/custom/coverage.dat

$ bazel coverage --action_env=CLASSPATH_LIMIT=100 //examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject:custom
...
//examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject:custom        PASSED in 0.6s
# No .dat file mentioned
$ ls -lh /home/ubuntu/.cache/bazel/_bazel_ubuntu/5bb6c1fa5da68b7db1883687715859ce/execroot/io_bazel/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/testlogs/examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject/custom/coverage.dat
-r-xr-xr-x 1 ubuntu ubuntu 0 Jul 27 16:27 /home/ubuntu/.cache/bazel/_bazel_ubuntu/5bb6c1fa5da68b7db1883687715859ce/execroot/io_bazel/bazel-out/k8-fastbuild/testlogs/examples/java-native/src/test/java/com/example/myproject/custom/coverage.dat
```

### What operating system are you running Bazel on?

Linux

### What's the output of `bazel info release`?

release 3.4.1

###  Have you found anything relevant by searching the web?

No :(

### Any other information, logs, or outputs that you want to share?

Workaround/Pointer to fix would be appreciated. I briefly looked at JacocoCoverageRunner.java but don't have enough context with this code to make progress quickly.
